claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks user-friendly onboarding, requiring players to search for information online or figure out controls through trial and error.

citations.review_text: Fun little community manager game, only downside is its not user friendly so you will be searching up a lot of specific things on your browser. But on the plus side it is extremely interactive and incredibly diverse. 8/10 worth the money.

Absolute recommend. Most of the reviews I have seen have thousands of hours of play time. You do not need a hundred hours to enjoy this game. I had fun from hour one, well, after I figured out the controls. It's fun to discover the different events and colonist attributes. I came to the game blind and am still blind to most things, but this game totally absorbs my attention and gives me great joy. 10/10 would buy again, even at full price.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that DLC pricing is high and predatory, with the total cost for all expansions exceeding one hundred dollars even during sales.

citations.review_text: DLC pricing and practices are predatory and sour what is otherwise a fantastic game that I would recommend in a heartbeat. The entire game is effectively designed and balanced around them but despite this they cost over $100 for no other reason than the developers know people will pay for them. If you want the game just buy the base game and figure out how to get the DLC elsewhere, the price you pay for that is how much the game + DLC should cost anyway. Good game and by all means buy the base game but please do not give in to practices like this just because the developer is indie, unless you're okay with the idea of indie games becoming indistinguishable from AAA with their practices. This game feels like a canary in a coal mine where it's not the worst thing in the world by itself but what it represents for the future feels very wrong and makes me uneasy.

It is a good game, but these dlc's are a problem. You can buy full games for the price of one of these things ON SALE, And EVERY worthwhile addition to this game seems to be locked behind one. Sure, if you've been with this since day one, it might not seem so bad, but even with every single one on sale, I gotta drop over a hundred bucks to actually get the full game. Can you at least drop a RW2 or anniversary addition with everything before odyssey built in before you add more overpriced dlc's.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a modding scene through the workshop that adds to the experience.

citations.review_text: Ridiculously fun with workshop mods!

Takes a bit to figure out what needs to be done as all colony sims do but it's extremely worth it once you figure stuff out. It's the kind of game that you'll want to start over and do it again once you learn something new because you see all the things that are holding you back.

Very fun! It's worth every penny (especially since the modding scene is robust).

I've played this game for a while now and i've enjoyed it the entire time. My timing couldn't have been better because 1.7 and the new Waylith engine has helped performance tremendously all while conserving mod/save file compatibility. I can only recommend this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the tutorial is very brief and basic, creating a steep learning curve before the game clicks.

citations.review_text: Playing the tutorial and one mission on the defaults settings took 61 hours and was thoroughly nail-biting fun. Definitely earns it's good reputation. I haven't tried any of the DLC yet, and probably shouldn't since this is so addictive it's disruptive.

There is a steep learning curve as the tutorial for the game is very brief and basic but once you start to figure things out it becomes extremely fun. 
I would recommend this to people who like to press all of the buttons and baubles in front of them just to see what they do; and to people who like restricting their colonists' diet to raw human flesh.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features extensive modding support and a large workshop community.

citations.review_text: I've enjoyed the game very much. It's a story generator and you have the option to leave, my personal favourite way is play to play with mods, the modding community is absolutely incredible too. Some people have made Rimworld's world map into a territory map which can represent different factions and plus it adds onto the story. I often find myself making new scenario's after finding the old one boring or having completed my plans for such a story. It's definetly worth a try!

One of the best games I've played. Very modding friendly, good attention to details in small places which is unexpected from modern gaming. Basically immortal due to high modding scene and insane support of modders. Surprisingly pro-player game, and is an example how games should be made. Highly recommend. Only issue is when you add like 20 mods it takes quite A LOT of time to start the game, though after you enter it is fairly responsive even with 100+ mods.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game engine update significantly improves performance and reduces loading times for heavily modded setups.

citations.review_text:
TYNAN I LOVE 1.7 YOU ARE THE GOAT
For a more detailed review, Rimworld is a colony simulator game. The base game is fun to play, however the primary strength of rimworld is that it is highly receptive to modding. Now for most games this raises another issue; Performance. When your colonists are having their mood simulated, the modded alien parasite hidden inside of them growing and a countdown to smart modded factions launching intelligent raids on you, the performance takes a hit. Pre 1.7 had the game running on unity which has it's own issues but in the unstable 1.7 branch it has been moved to the developer's own engine and performance has massively increased.  This goes to show that even if you have a game with years of spaghetti code it can still have performance fixes. Looking at you, Stellaris.

Look at the time I've played this, first off. This is how long I've clocked BEFORE 1.7's new Waylith Engine. I would've given this game a 5/5 rating anyway and not thought twice. Now? I've got about 1500 mods which USED to take 45 minutes to load with startup optimizing mods but with 1.7 it's taken about as long to boot as I've spent writing this review. No other game has had such an immense fundamental upgrade that wasn't a content drop. This solidly makes Rimworld one of the greatest games of it's kind.

Honestly the game is fantastic I love playing with mods though and the new engine is INSANE INCREASE TO PERFORMANCE I used to not be able to run the Progression modlist it took 40 minutes to load and no frames due to my computer specs. Now I can RUN THAT LIST AT 170 FPS AVERAGE! and no mods broke absolutely phenomenal job I don't know any other studio that could pull of such a feat.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that DLC pricing is prohibitively expensive.

citations.review_text: The DLC pricing is not ok, no matter how good the game is.

A story generator that can only generate a single story and a colony sim that mistakes tedious micromanagement for depth, no matter how many dlcs (which are prohibitely expensive and mostly just add more crap to manage without making the game any more deep) or mods you run every playthrough will largely go and end the same way, you will build the same base every time and either escape the planet waow or get swarmed by an army of pirates with doomsday launchers or mechanoids because you have too many expensive doodads lying around in your base and die. 
There is more to talk about with how the storytellers dont actually tell a story and are just a bunch of rng checks so nothing happens for a reason except the computer decided its time for it to happen or how all pawns are basically the same and all the backstories are just stat modifiers that sometimes add quirks that are just another tedious thing you have to manage around and all of the story and interactions basically happen in your head because in game they are just another set of rng checks.
